description: A creative hackathon team combining coding, AI, and space technology to build innovative solutions and explore new frontiers. 🚀
summary: Many people believe the space crafts we sent into space are dead and forgotten. Abandoned but Not Forgotten shows that the story is more interesting. It is an educational website that compiles 40 robotic missions into one archive, from Apollo hardware on the Moon to the Voyagers in interstellar space. Every machine has an honest status (Active, Lost, etc.) and a link to a NASA source. We want students and curious people to see what humanity sent, what we learned and that some of these machines are still talking.
details:
How it functions: The website is based on four locations: Moon, Mars, Earth orbit, and deep space. All 40 missions come from a single data set which produces the location pages, the searchable archive (filtered by location, time, type, and state), and the counters. Voyager 1 and 2 have dedicated pages with timelines and comparison tables. Each mission links to a public NASA source, and if something is not clear about its location or fate, the website states so instead of making assumptions.
Tools: The website took advantage of HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript along with Three.js and GLTFLoader for creating the 3D scene and was implemented in one file with no need to use any building steps and any special hardware. Claude, Codex, and Gemini were involved in generating texts, coding, bug-fixing and brainstorming for the project.
Creativity: An interactive 3D figure, procedural textures of Earth and Moon, and an animated signal wave.
Factors we took into account: Accuracy, accessibility (keyboard navigation, support for reduced motion), mobile-friendly design, and independence from NASA.
